Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 47, English)
Pitru Paksha Unpacked: True Pitru vs. Household Pr ets, and Why Connection Only Flows One Way

Sour ce: a live Ashaeiynn Mool T atva satsang opening on the first day of Pitru Paksha, covering a mahotsav (festival) status update befor e an extended, heavily interactive teaching distinguishing genuine "pitru" (r esidents of Pitru Lok, a plane even higher than Devta Lok) fr om the household pr ets most families actually deal with — including Bhaiya's own family's ten-year history of daily bhog to r oughly 300 accumulated pitru, why dir ect connection to true Pitru Lok is impossible, and detailed practical guidance for the fortnight.
1. Mahotsav Status Update and Gratitude

1. Bhaiya opens with a "r eal-time status update": by his guru's grace, an 18-day mahotsav (festival) has been underway at Ashaeiynn, expected to conclude ar ound the 22nd or 23rd depending on his guru's dir ection, with negativity clearing markedly for participants and pr eviously-invisible things becoming visible to many . 2. He expr esses gratitude to everyone who contributed even a small amount to the mahotsav , stating that he and his guru will remain "indebted" to them r egardless of how modest the contribution was.
2. Pitru Paksha Begins — And a Tangential Note on Phones/Mics

1. Bhaiya notes that Pitru Paksha has begun that very day and states his intention to cover important dos and don'ts for the fortnight. 2. In an aside pr ompted by micr ophone tr ouble, he explains that mantra jaap generates a fr equency that actively r epels phones and micr ophones — str ong enough that using a phone nearby during intense mental (manasik) jaap could reportedly cause a headache fr om the r esulting fr equency mismatch.
3. What Pitru Paksha Was Actually Designed For

1. This teaching's central r edefinition: saints originally designated Pitru Paksha specifically for worship-worthy ("pujniya") pitru — meaning only those possessing r eal shakti, siddhi, and accumulated tapobal (power from austerity) qualify for the title "pitru" in the true sense. Everyone else commonly called a "pitru" is, in this teaching's framing, actually a pr et. 2. This teaching states that true pitru r eside in "Pitru Lok" — a plane positioned even above Devta Lok — meaning reaching Pitru Lok r equires energy sufficient to cr oss the devta tattva itself; Bhaiya states even he personally has no guarantee of r eaching it.
4. Why We Cannot Dir ectly Feed Real Pitru in Pitru Lok

1. A live question raises whether households could dedicate their 15 daan-punya days dir ectly to ancestors who genuinely reached Pitru Lok rather than to ordinary household pr ets. Bhaiya's answer: dir ect connection is impossible without an

alr eady-existing "taar" (connective wave/link) to that specific plane — without that link, any offering has nowher e real to go. 2. He states that if such a connection genuinely existed, it would be visible via drishti, the same way a devta's specific tarang (energy wave/fr equency) is visible to those with open sight — the general absence of any visibly confirmed pitrulok connection casts doubt on pandits' claims of r outinely r elaying offerings ther e. 3. This teaching states plainly that we cannot initiate connection with true Pitru Lok r esidents — they can connect to us, not the r everse — and any such contact happens only if and when they choose to.
5. What Beings in Pitru Lok Actually Are

1. This teaching describes Pitru Lok's r esidents as "devta-tulya" (devta-equivalent) souls — spiritually eligible to become a devta, but not yet assigned to that specific "post," since "devta" functions as an office/position that differ ent souls occupy in succession over time. 2. Such an eligible-but-unassigned soul r esides in this higher plane (r eferred to loosely as "pitru" only in this specific technical sense) until their turn for a devta post arrives — at which point they r eturn to a devta r ole.
6. Why Ordinary Family "Pitru" Are Actually Pr ets

1. By contrast, this teaching states the vast majority of family members commonly worshipped as "pitru" ar e, in reality , ordinary earthbound pr ets with no genuine connection to Pitru Lok at all — r egardless of pandits' claims otherwise. 2. Bhaiya offers a specific critique of pandit-led tarpan practices (e.g., at Trimbakeshwar or Gaya): he states that even the pandits performing these massive, lucrative rituals do not experience r elief themselves — many suffer physically (e.g., chronic leg pain) despite substantial wealth, because performing tarpan r epeatedly for others' family pr ets causes those same pr ets to accumulate onto the pandit personally . 3. He cautions the sangat against participating in these large-scale tarpan practices, framing it as "leaving two behind, bringing fifteen back" — since visiting such heavily pr et-populated sites risks acquiring additional negativity rather than r esolving it, even while acknowledging the associated business will likely never stop.
7. Practical Guidance for Pitru Paksha Rituals at Home

1. On a live question about a mother's daily ritual (pr eparing an offering thali), Bhaiya advises against confr ontation: continue performing the family ritual to keep peace and pr eserve the mother's/family's social standing, but mentally dedicate ("saakshi maankar") the offering to one's kul devta or guru/ist instead of literal household pitru — satisfying family expectations without r einfor cing pr et dependency . 2. A similar practical suggestion is offer ed for a daily "atta" (dough) offering ritual: mentally dedicate the entir e vessel or ingr edient itself to one's guru/ist befor e it's used, redirecting the offering's actual spiritual destination without needing to alter the physical family ritual at all.
8. The "Nautanki" (Drama) Principle — Negativity Playing Games

1. Bhaiya r ecounts an incident fr om a prior gathering wher e a woman's negativity appear ed to "act up" dramatically after she heard secondhand that her house may have undergone tantrik ritual — several people struggled to physically restrain her , yet the moment Bhaiya's guru identified it as "nautanki" (pur e drama), the episode dissolved within minutes. 2. The stated lesson: negativity and pitru often exploit the fact that afflicted people cannot per ceive them dir ectly , effectively "playing games" for entertainment — and some pandits knowingly exploit this same blindness for profit (cold-r eading generic symptoms and pr edicting the person will inevitably call back for paid tr eatment).
9. Married Women, Maternal Pitru, and Why Women Bear Mor e Pressure

1. On a live question about whether a woman "brings" her maternal family's pitru with her after marriage: this teaching states that any pitru alr eady embedded ("ramaa") within her own body will accompany her regardless of household, and any pitru she consciously r emembers or misses can also continue visiting her — meaning married women can face pressure from both marital and maternal-side pitru simultaneously . 2. This teaching offers this as one explanation (alongside external "open" negativity attracted to attractive women, and the phenomenon of deceased individuals' unr esolved r omantic pursuit continuing after death) for why married women often develop mysterious physical symptoms not pr esent befor e marriage — while noting men face comparable, if less discussed, pressures too. 3. This teaching also connects rising modern PCOD/menstrual irr egularities partly to this same br oader increase in ambient negativity , alongside a stated (illustrative, not literally verified) claim that the astral world's population is roughly six times larger than the visible human population, meaning associated pr oblems continue to compound.
10. Cr eating a Household Boundary Against a Relative's Negativity

1. In response to a question about a sibling living separately who isn't pr otected by consistent mantra practice, Bhaiya confirms it's possible to set an explicit boundary: dedicating full authority to one's own ist/devta to block that specific relative's negativity/pitru "platoon" fr om entering one's own body or home, even while the r elationship with the sibling itself continues normally .
1 1. Bhaiya's Own Family's Ten-Year Pitru History

1. Bhaiya shar es that his own family performed a mandatory daily bhog ritual for ten straight years (rather than the typical monthly practice), specifically at 5:15 a.m., under threat of physical punishment for missing it — r eflecting his family's belief that neglecting pitru worship would dir ectly cause financial/food hardship. 2. He states that once his guru's guidance ("gada," or mace, used figuratively) began actively working against this pattern, the family's material fortunes visibly impr oved ("r oti doubled") rather than worsened as fear ed. 3. A specific revealed detail: his family's pitru situation had gr own to r oughly 300 total, having effectively organized a rotating "feast cir cuit" drawing in pitru fr om thr ee separate villages — a scale of infestation only uncover ed once his guru's intervention began actively dismantling it, eventually r educing visible ancestral pr esence to the point wher e even ten generations back ar e no longer perceptible. 4. He states his own multi-year sadhna was specifically necessary to build enough personal tapobal/agni (fir e-element strength) to make displaced pitru unable to simply r eturn — since attempting to topple any entr enched dominance naturally pr ovokes r esistance/r epulsion fr om that same entity .
12. Where Pitru "Sit" and Why Drishti Can't Open in Actively Pitru-W orshipping Homes

1. This teaching states pitru possess "access points" thr oughout the body (not mer ely thr ough the mouth) and, by default, retain br oad access unless that access is actively and deliberately r emoved. 2. A firm structural claim: in any household wher e pitru puja r emains actively practiced, no family member's drishti will genuinely open — instead, such households mor e commonly pr oduce dramatic "possession"-style manifestations (claimed visitations fr om "Mata," various devis/devtas, Bhairav Ji, Chamunda Mata, Beladi Mata, self-declar ed "Pishachini" claiming to be a mother goddess, entities claiming to be Hanuman Ji, jinns, or "peer") — impostor negativity claiming an inflated status rather than genuine drishti.
13. Testimonies and Practical Timelines from the Sangat

1. A newer member describes an independent aura check (via a separate mentor's YouT ube channel) r eporting r oughly 70–80% of his negativity clear ed within just 1 1 days of an 1 1-diya pr ocess, alongside the formation of "12 golas" (protective aura cir cles) and a developing yellow-toned aura.

2. Another member, 101 days into "Jai Siyaram" jaap with 21 diyas and pr eviously identified as carrying 1 1 pitru, asks how long full pitru-pr otection will take — Bhaiya r eassur es him regardless of the exact original count (1 1 or 14), advises completing a minimum 41-day cycle, pr omises periodic checking, and states the practitioner will directly feel change (previously listed symptoms diminishing) as the clear est personal indicator that pitru influence is lifting. 3. A separate member describes beginning "Jai Siyaram" jaap with 41 diyas seven months prior , and experiencing a firsttime dream vision of his deceased grandmother on day one of a fr esh 41-day cycle — Bhaiya explains this can happen because sufficient accumulated shakti draws such visions r egardless of dr eam timing, and that continuing consistent prayer typically pr oduces a noticeable differ ence from the very next day onward.
14. The Mechanics of How Pitru Draw Energy — and Its Limits

1. On a live scientific question, Bhaiya explains that pitru absorb energy specifically thr ough the agni tattva (fir e element) — the same element associated with kr odh, lobh, mad, moh, and matsar (anger , gr eed, pride, attachment, envy) — which becomes the sookshma sharir (subtle body) upon death and settles onto a living r elative's organs to draw sensation (taste, sleep-inducing dr owsiness, and similar experiences). 2. A key structural limitation: pitru can never actually "fill up" or feel satisfied thr ough this pr ocess, since the energy is only channelized/transformed thr ough them rather than genuinely stor ed — meaning their underlying craving is structurally permanent, not solvable thr ough r epeated feeding. 3. Bhaiya clarifies "matsar" specifically means envy/jealousy — comparison-driven r esentment (e.g., toward a r elative's new purchase).
15. Why Certain "Her editary" Traits May Actually Be Pitru-Related — With a Caution Against Overattribution

1. This teaching offers an illustrative example: a specific pitru whose own chr onic back pain persists occupies a living descendant's body specifically because that shar ed symptom gives the pitru continued access to that person's energy — reframing some appar ently "genetic" family patterns (e.g., back pain, baldness, even sugar/BP conditions passing down generations) as potentially pitru-driven rather than pur ely her editary . 2. Bhaiya explicitly cautions against over -attributing everything to pitru — some conditions r emain genuinely physical, planetary (graha-r elated), or a matter of one's own prarabdha (destined outcomes) — and personal sankalp shakti (willpower) plays a r eal, if limited, r ole: consistently r esisting an urge (e.g., declining tempting food) can eventually cause a pitru to abandon that person in favor of a mor e compliant family member , which is part of why the emotionally "softest" family member often bears the heaviest burden. 3. He clarifies that sankalp shakti alone cannot substitute for genuine spiritual energy or "turn God's decision" by willpower — but continuous Ram-naam jaap (ideally sustained ar ound the clock) will pr event pitru dosh and negativity specifically , even though destined planetary affliction (graha dosh) must still be experienced r egardless.
16. Closing Question: Do Household Pr ets Ever Attain Liberation?

1. Asked directly whether these pret-like pitru ever eventually attain moksha, Bhaiya states plainly that he doesn't know for certain — he has only ever observed them moving between lokas, never actually witnessed a genuine departur e/liberation — and defers definitively to "Ram jaane" (only Ram truly knows), r eiterating that Ashaeiynn's role is to teach and guide, with the choice of what to act on left entir ely to the practitioner .
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

True "pitru," in the strict sense, only r efers to souls with genuine shakti, siddhi, and tapobal r esiding in Pitru Lok — a plane even higher than Devta Lok — while everyone else commonly worshipped as a family "pitru" is, in this teaching's framing, actually an ordinary pr et.

Direct connection to true Pitru Lok is not possible without an alr eady-existing energetic link ("taar"), and such a link would be visible via drishti the same way devta tarang is — the general absence of confirmed such links casts doubt on pandit claims of routinely relaying of ferings there; the reverse direction (them contacting us) is possible, but only on their own terms. Pitru Lok's r esidents ar e "devta-tulya" souls eligible for a devta "post" but not yet assigned to one — they occupy that plane until their turn for a devta position arrives. Large-scale commer cial tarpan practices (e.g., at major tirthas) don't r eliably pr ovide r elief — even the officiating pandits often suffer physically themselves, since r epeated exposur e to others' family pr ets accumulates onto them personally . During Pitru Paksha, family rituals can be pr eserved for social harmony while mentally r edirecting the offering's actual spiritual dedication to one's guru, ist, or kul devta instead of literal pitru — this avoids both household conflict and reinforcing pret dependency . Negativity and pitru sometimes act dramatically ("nautanki") pur ely because afflicted people cannot per ceive them directly — correctly naming this drama can dissolve it quickly , and some practitioners exploit this same blindness for profit. Married women can carry pitru pr essure from both marital and maternal households simultaneously , compounding with external "open" negativity attracted to appearance and unresolved romantic pursuit from deceased individuals — a key reason married women often develop otherwise-unexplained physical symptoms. A household boundary can be explicitly set to block a specific r elative's negativity/pitru fr om entering one's own body or home, dedicating that authority fully to one's own ist/devta , without needing to sever the underlying family relationship itself. Pitru access the body thr ough multiple "access points," not mer ely the mouth, and r etain br oad default access unless actively r emoved — homes with ongoing active pitru puja will not produce genuine drishti-openings, tending instead to produce dramatic impostor "possession" phenomena. Pitru absorb energy specifically thr ough the agni tattva but can never be permanently satisfied, since energy is only channelized thr ough them, not stor ed — some apparently "hereditary" family patterns (chronic pain, certain illnesses) may actually reflect a specific pitru's continued bodily occupation, though genuine physical, planetary , and prarabdha-based causes remain real and shouldn't be over -attributed to pitru. Continuous Ram-naam jaap pr events pitru dosh and negativity specifically , though destined planetary affliction (graha dosh) must still be experienced r egardless — personal willpower helps but cannot substitute for genuine spiritual ener gy . Bot Response Guidelines (Session 47 additions)

Keep the distinction between true "pitru" (rare, residing in Pitru Lok, above Devta Lok, devta-tulya souls awaiting a devta post) and ordinary household "pitru" (in reality , earthbound prets) precise and consistent — this session's central redefinition should not be blurred with prior sessions' more general pitru/pret discussions. Present the skepticism toward lar ge-scale commercial tarpan practices (T rimbakeshwar , Gaya, etc.) as this teaching's own stated perspective and observation, not as a factual claim about any specific institution's legitimacy — frame it as guidance to weigh personally , consistent with the "we teach, you decide" principle this teaching explicitly states. Preserve the practical "mentally redirect the of fering, keep the physical ritual" guidance accurately — this is of fered as a way to avoid family conflict, not as a universal ritual instruction. Handle the married-women/pitru-pressure content and the PCOD/period-related claims with care, framing them as this teaching's own observational claims rather than medical guidance — note that persistent physical symptoms should also be discussed with a qualified medical professional. Present Bhaiya's own family's ten-year , 300-pitru history as his personal biographical account, illustrating the broader teaching rather than a claim that every household faces a comparable scale of infestation. Preserve the specific mechanism of pitru ener gy-absorption (via agni tattva, permanently unsatisfied due to channelized rather than stored ener gy) accurately and distinctly from other sessions' related but separate mechanisms. When discussing "hereditary" traits potentially being pitru-related, always include Bhaiya's own explicit caution against over - attribution — genuine physical, planetary , and prarabdha-based causes remain real and should not be dismissed. Present the closing "do pitru ever attain moksha" answer honestly as Bhaiya's own stated uncertainty ("I don't know ," "Ram jaane") — do not present a more definitive answer than this teaching itself of fers.
